newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Electric snubs China Light proposal.
newsitem.headline: HK Electric snubs China Light proposal.

text.p: Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd (HEC) on Tuesday rejected a plan by competitor China Light & Power Co Ltd (CLP) to buy its excess power as that would disrupt supply of electricity to its own customers.
"HEC considers the CLP proposal to sell electricity to HEC through the existing interconnectors is neither viable nor justifiable and HEC will not buy power from CLP," HEC said in a statement.

If existing interconnectors, which are designed for emergency back-up and economic transfer, were used to transfer the large, steady supply of electricity to HEC as proposed by China Light, security of supply to customers would be disrupted, it added.
China Light has come under pressure to halt or defer the commissioning of four units at its eight-plant Black Point power station due to a slow growth in electricity demand.
The Hong Kong government asked the company last November to submit a report on the costs of deferring units five to eight of the plant after experts recommended a delay of original plans.

But in its report, China Light said deferral would cost some HK$200 million to over HK$1.5 billion in additional costs and gave other proposals for the government to consider, amongst them a plan to transfer the excess power to HEC.
But HEC snubbed the plan in its tersely-worded statement.
"If the interconnectors are used to supply a firm load to HEC, such decoupling will result in power interrruption to a large number of HEC's consumers," it said.
"Imagine people trapped in lifts, life-supporting machines stopping or the Stock Exchange supply being suspended."
In an initial response to China Light's report, the government said in a statement more details were needed before an assessment of the proposals could be made.
"CLP's report lacked certain key information to enable the government to assess whether the company's proposals were in the best interests of consumers," the statement said.
